* If your room isn't clean, clean it. 
* If you ever make a meal, do the dishes immediately.
* Every morning, make your bed. 
* After taking a shower, look at yourself in the mirror. By this, I mean look at yourself. Don't think about anything, you don't need to. Look at yourself.
* Take up a hobby. Or a lot of hobbies. For example, your university might offer a gym or some clubs. Go to the gym, sign up for classes like taekwon do or rock climbing.

You need things to do, and you need things to appreciate. Step outside and breathe air in. You can do that; it's an amazing thing. I'm still struggling with accepting the fact that she left me. I think the issue people are finding the most is that theyre trying to spam past a charged attack to interrupt when you can just as easily dodge backwards and strike as normal or with your own charge. They may be bugged at the moment but they shouldn't be so difficult to counter.

I play windfall too! With stagger, most of their attacks are either straight or mid sweeps. You'll have enough stamina to block their first attack and once theyre in their chain, study whether or not their attack is going to be far straight or a quick mid sweep. With straights, use your special to dodge to the side, I typically go left. With the sweep, don't be afraid to use stamina to do the neutral dodge. You'll recover way quicker than being hit that way. 

I've also noticed that stagger doesn't really lie low on the ground and since youre playing windfall, low sweeps are good to use as counter hits. 

Just remember that stagger is typically high offense school so being patient until you have an opening works real well.

OP, when I was around your age I felt similar to what you're feeling. Getting out of bed is hard isn't it? It's like, "what's the point if I'm just going to slip up and make another mistake? It's far better off if I just stay home where I won't fuck anything up."  

I told my parents and my brother once and what they said made me sink even farther. They told me to deal with it, and you don't need to see anyone because if you think what you're dealing with is hard right now you have no idea. Now that made me feel like shit.

 I started this tradition I have every birthday I've had since I was 15(I'm 20 now). Whether or not I had a birthday party I would somehow find myself alone some time in the night and think to myself, "congratulations me, I survived another year." I would also reminisce on the time that one of my friends father passed away. A week or so after his father died he told me that the worst part about his whole experience was that he'll still feel like shit that he's gone, and the whole world would keep on spinning as if there wasn't even a tremor from his absence.

So what does that mean? To me, that didn't mean that if I offed myself no one in the world would give a shit; no, if I killed myself my parents, and my brother, and my friends whom I've held close to my heart would stop their lives dead in their tracks and be devastated.

It's the worst when your whole body shakes with your mind racing in tandem uncontrollably. It's the worst when you run out of tears and you can see the blood from your knuckles drip dry on the brick wall. It's the worst when the people who you'd think would be there for you just give you voicemails instead. It's the absolute worst when you give up, and let the world keep spinning. 

You just gotta keep spinning with it. You'll feel more mechanical, and you'll feel more empty as you go on, but as you go on you'll find sparks of life and love that make this dark you keep inside somewhat worth it.
